THE CAT IN THE OPENING: a small cat sitting dead centre in the shadow of the great arch, tail wrapped around its paws, plainly unbothered by the entire arrival pressing in around it
THE CAT ON THE SUNNY STONE: a small orange cat stretched full-length along a warm stone at the wall's foot, one ear twitching, deeply asleep in a patch of gold light
THE CAT ON THE LEDGE: a small tortoiseshell cat draped along the warm ledge above the arch, tiny in the frame, one paw dangling, watching nothing in particular with supreme indifference
THE CAT ON THE CART TAIL: a small black cat sitting upright on a cart's tail beside the gate, tail curled, watching the archway with the focused air of someone who owns it
THE CAT AT THE DRAIN: a small tabby cat crouched at the wall's foot with one paw pressed deep into a drain hole cut low in the stone, fishing for something with absolute concentration
THE ROW ON THE TEETH: a long row of small white birds settled tight along the square stone teeth at the top of the wall, every beak tucked the same way, tiny and orderly against the sky
THE TWO ON THE BRACKET: two fat pigeons small on a lamp bracket above the gate passage, puffed to twice their size, leaning shoulder to shoulder like old friends sharing a secret
THE NEST IN THE SLIT: a nest of sticks crammed into a slit window high in the wall, a small bright-eyed head poking over the rim, watching the road below with proprietorial calm
THE FLOCK LIFTING: a flock of small birds lifting all together off the parapet, tiny against the rooftops above, each one a quick dark comma spinning up into the open air
THE BIRD ON THE RIDGE: a long-legged bird standing on one leg on the roof ridge above the gate, small and perfectly still, silhouetted flat and dark against the bright sky
THE DOG IN THE WAY: a small dog flat out asleep in the exact middle of the way through the gate, side-on and tiny against the stone, determined to be the last thing moved today
THE TROTTING DOG: a scruffy small dog trotting side-on along the wall's foot with something long and improbable in its mouth, moving with the brisk purpose of a creature running late
THE THREE DUCKS: three small ducks crossing the trodden ground in a wobbly line, the last one always a step behind, making their way toward the trough with total self-importance
THE GOAT ON THE DRIFT: a small goat side-on up on the rubble drift at the wall's foot, eating a big mouthful out of somebody's straw hat, wearing an expression of complete civic satisfaction
THE CARP IN THE MOAT: three big bright carp holding still in the moat water at mid-distance, their orange and white shapes clear and slow below the surface, watching the reflection of the gate
THE TIPPED DUCKS: two small ducks beside the moat stone, both tipped straight tail-up at once, their bright feet pedalling the air above the water's surface in perfect comic unison
THE HERON LIFTING: a heron lifting off low across the moat water, small against the far stone, wings opening in one long slow pull, trailing its feet behind it like an afterthought
THE TURTLE ON THE STONE: a small turtle small on a stone at the water's edge, shell domed and bright, neck stretched long to catch the warmth, entirely at peace with the traffic above
THE FOX ON THE WALKWAY: a small fox sitting up on the wall's walkway at the far end of the gate, tiny in the frame, ears pricked, looking out at the road below with amber-eyed curiosity
THE CAT ON THE STAIR: a small striped cat halfway up the outside stair of the gatehouse tower, frozen mid-step, staring back at something below with theatrical alarm at nothing visible
THE SWIFTS ON THE TOWER: a family of small swifts turning round one tower in a fast bright loop, each one a black dash, the whole group turning all together as one
THE SPARROW IN THE TROUGH: a small sparrow splashing hard in the trough beside the gate wall, scattering bright drops in a wide arc, shaking itself with the vigour of someone making a point
THE PIGEON ON THE STEP: a plump small pigeon parading along the broad front step of the gate, head bobbing with enormous ceremony, inspecting every crack as though taking formal inventory
THE STARLING ON THE BRACKET: a small starling perched on a lamp bracket, feathers lit up green and violet, turning its head sharply side to side with bright suspicion
THE WREN IN THE SHADOW: a tiny wren flickering out of the archway's shadow and back in again, tiny in the frame, too fast to follow, a small warm dart in the dark of the stone
